## QUESTION 1

__Use the provided code above to read in the batting table. Then, with Python Polars manipulate the 'results' dataframe to calculate the number of at bats and the batting average for each year a player played. Filter the data frame to only include players with at least 10 at bats that year. Sort the dataframe from highest batting average to lowest, and then by playerid alphabetically. Show the top 5 results in your report.__

Note: A batting average is meant to measure how often a player puts the ball in play and gets to base safely. For this task, use a simplified version of batting average defined as the sum of hits (labeled 'H') divided by number of at bats (labeled 'AB').

_The below table has aggregated players to ensure there are no duplicates, and calculated each individual's batting average. It has eliminated anyone with less than ten times at bat to prevent skewed data. As seen in the batting average column, the highest batting average is a little over 60% of the time. Also noted is most of these high hitters are in the 20th century rather than now. This could indicate a change in modern baseball tactics or rules._

```{python}
adf = (
  results.group_by(["playerID", "yearID"])
  .agg(
    pl.col("H").sum(),
    pl.col("AB").sum()
  )
  .filter(pl.col("AB")>=10)
  .with_columns((pl.col("H")/pl.col("AB")).alias("batting_average"))
  .sort(by=["batting_average","playerID"],descending=[True,False])
  .with_columns(pl.col("batting_average").round(3))
)
adf.head(5)
```


## QUESTION 2

__Use the provided code above to read in the batting table. Then, with Python Polars manipulate the 'results' dataframe to calculate the batting average for each player over their entire career (all years combined). Only include players with at least 100 at bats over their entire career. Sort the dataframe from highest batting average to lowest, and then by playerid alphabetically. Show the top 5 results in your report.__ 

Note: A batting average is meant to measure how often a player puts the ball in play and gets to base safely. For this task, use a simplified version of batting average defined as the sum of hits (labeled 'H') divided by number of at bats (labeled 'AB').

_This table has also calculated batting average, but over a player's entire career. This table is much more accurate to a player's ability rather than just having a good year. It has removed any player with less than 100 times at bat to exclude outliers. As seen in the batting average column, a player's hit percentage is much lower, all top players at around a 35% hit rate. This lower average could indicate that the first table was a collection of player's highlight years rather than their actual skill. It is of note that the numbers for top players at bat are much higher than the filtration minumum of 100 times. This could indicate that players who have such an average were known to be good players and were therefore sent to bat more often._

```{python}
adf = (
  results.group_by(["playerID"])
  .agg(
    pl.col("H").sum(),
    pl.col("AB").sum()
  )
  .filter(pl.col("AB")>=100)
  .with_columns((pl.col("H")/pl.col("AB")).alias("batting_average"))
  .sort(by=["batting_average","playerID"],descending=[True,False])
  .with_columns(pl.col("batting_average").round(3))
)
adf.head(5)
```
